categories.main_business_segments: Acadia Healthcare operates four main business segments: acute inpatient psychiatric facilities, specialty treatment facilities (including residential recovery and eating disorder centers), comprehensive treatment centers (CTCs) specializing in medication-assisted opioid treatment, and residential treatment centers for behavioral disorders. Outpatient programs are included within each respective service line.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company delivers behavioral healthcare through a medical delivery model that incorporates structured and intensive medical and behavioral therapies, 24-hour monitoring by psychiatrists and trained staff, and individualized treatment plans. Treatment modalities include medication-assisted therapy, cognitive/behavioral therapies, group and individual counseling, and a continuum of care from inpatient to outpatient services.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Acadia primarily serves individuals with mental health and substance use disorders, including adults, adolescents, and children with high-acuity or complex needs. Key customers include state Medicaid programs, commercial insurers, Medicare, and self-pay patients, with a focus on high-need populations such as those with opioid use disorder and serious mental illness.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of December 31, 2022, Acadia operated 250 facilities with approximately 11,000 beds across 39 U.S. states and Puerto Rico. The company previously operated in the UK but divested those operations in 2021 to focus exclusively on the U.S. market.
categories.supply_chain_position: Acadia operates as a downstream provider, delivering direct patient care at the point of service within the healthcare supply chain. The company owns and manages behavioral healthcare facilities and outpatient centers, interacting directly with patients and payors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include organic growth through facility expansions and bed additions, accelerated joint venture partnerships, de novo facility development, targeted acquisitions, and broadening the continuum of care, especially for substance use disorders. The company emphasizes operational efficiency, leveraging management expertise, and expanding access to underserved populations.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through fee-for-service payments for patient care, with reimbursement from Medicaid (51%), commercial insurers (30%), Medicare (15%), and self-pay/other sources (4%). The company also receives government grants and relief funds, such as those related to COVID-19, when applicable.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Acadia is the leading publicly traded pure-play provider of behavioral healthcare services in the U.S., operating in a highly fragmented and competitive industry. Major competitors include Universal Health Services (UHS), other behavioral health companies, general hospitals with mental health services, and private equity-backed providers. Acadia differentiates itself through scale, geographic diversity, and a focus on behavioral health.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2022, Acadia reported $2.61 billion in revenue, up 12.8% from the prior year, with net income of $273 million. The company has demonstrated consistent growth through acquisitions, facility expansions, and increased patient days, and maintains a strong financial position with significant cash flow and access to credit.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Acadia emphasizes high-quality, cost-effective behavioral healthcare with a broad geographic footprint, diversified payor and patient base, and a full continuum of care for complex and high-acuity patients. Its scale, experienced management team, and focus on operational excellence and access expansion position it as a preferred provider in a growing market with increasing demand for behavioral health services.
